raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

I've been doing wheat-maize on these 10 mu for as long as I can remember. It's just me and the wife now — our boy works off-farm, so we've got to keep things manageable. I'm 55, still strong enough, but I can't be breaking my back trying to do everything by hand like my father did.

**Wheat** — I got it in the ground back in early October, like always. Planted around the 8th, used the local variety I've been growing for years. At base I put down about 50 kg of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind from the cooperative shop) per mu, maybe a touch more. Come March at jointing I'll topdress about 15-20 kg of urea per mu, depending how the crop looks. The extension station says 15 kg N is enough, but I usually go a bit over — better to waste a little money than lose yield. Last year I got about 470 kg/mu so I'm aiming around 480 this year.

Irrigation — three times is my rule. Winter water before the freeze, jointing water in spring, and one more at grain filling. The well runs deep and the electric bill hurts, but skipping jointing water costs you 50 kg/mu easy, that's not a trade I'll make. Herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray once.

Harvest around June 10th. Then we're scrambling — between wheat combine and maize planter the window is maybe 5 days. I rent both machines from the village cooperative, no time for plowing, just straight no-till into the stubble.

**Maize** — I plant hybrid seed (Zhengdan 958 usually, or whatever the shop has that year), can't save it like wheat. Goes in mid-June. Same fertilizer plan roughly — 40 kg compound at planting, 15 kg urea topdress at knee-high stage. A bit less N than wheat because the wheat straw feeds the soil some.

Irrigation depends on the summer rains. Most years I water once or twice in July if it's dry. Some years I don't water at all. Pesticide — herbicide after emergence, and watch for corn borer. Last year was bad so I'll probably spray once. Harvest late September, about 500 kg/mu if things go well.

My wife and I can handle the field work between us, but at wheat harvest I'll hire a couple days of help to load the grain and get the maize in the ground on time. That's worth the money.
